fields.title: Kynance Cove to Lizard Point Coastal Trail
fields.description:
A stunning coastal walk along the most southerly point of mainland Britain. This dramatic route takes you from the turquoise waters of Kynance Cove, past serpentine rock formations, to the iconic Lizard Lighthouse. Marvel at the rugged clifftops, hidden coves, and if you're lucky, spot seals basking on the rocks below. The walk offers breathtaking views across Mount's Bay and is particularly spectacular at sunset. Along the way, you'll pass the Devil's Bellows blowhole and enjoy panoramic views of the Atlantic Ocean. Perfect for nature lovers and photographers alike.


Best visited during spring and summer when wildflowers carpet the clifftops. The Lizard RNLI station offers tea rooms open April-October. Strong winds are common in winter - check weather before setting out. Some sections can be muddy after rain.



Starting Point: Kynance Cove Car Park, Lizard Peninsula, Cornwall TR12 7PG

Walking Directions:

Stage 1: Kynance Cove to Caberthаh Beach 

  1. Exit the car park and head towards Kynance Cove beach
  2. Descend the steep path down to the cove (approximately 100 steps)
  3. Walk across Kynance Cove beach towards the right side
  4. Climb the rocky path up from the cove (marked with waymarkers)
  5. Continue along the coastal path heading south
  6. Pass the impressive serpentine rock formations on your right
  7. The path curves around to Caberthан Beach - continue upwards past the beach

Stage 2: Caberthан to Polpeor Cove 

  1. Keep following the coastal path south with the sea on your right
  2. Watch for the Devil's Bellows blowhole on your left (marked with a sign)
  3. Pass over several small rocky outcrops - stay on the main path
  4. Continue south towards Polpeor Cove
  5. The path descends slightly then climbs again
  6. You'll see Polpeor Cove below you on the right

Stage 3: Polpeor Cove to Lizard Lighthouse 

  1. Continue on the coastal path heading south
  2. Pass Polpeor Cove on your right (excellent photo spot)
  3. Keep following the cliff-edge path - it's well-marked with stone waymarkers
  4. The path gradually climbs as you approach the southernmost point
  5. You'll see the iconic red and white striped Lizard Lighthouse ahead
  6. Follow the path as it curves right towards the lighthouse
  7. Arrive at the Lizard Point visitor area (tea rooms and facilities)

fields.title: Porthleven Harbour to Praa Sands Clifftop Trail
fields.description:
Discover the charming fishing village of Porthleven and its dramatic coastal surroundings on this scenic clifftop walk. This route combines working harbour views, golden sandy beaches, and spectacular Atlantic Ocean vistas. Porthleven is one of Cornwall's most picturesque harbours with colourful fishing boats and excellent seafood restaurants. The walk takes you past the historic lighthouse, along dramatic cliffs, and down to the beautiful Praa Sands beach - a Blue Flag award-winning beach perfect for swimmers and surfers.

Walking Directions:

Stage 1: Porthleven Harbour Circuit Start at Porthleven Harbour car park Walk towards the harbour front with the water on your right Follow the promenade past the fishing boats and restaurants Walk around the harbour edge to the historic Porthleven Lighthouse Continue past the lighthouse following the coastal path Climb the rocky path upwards away from the harbour Reach the cliff-top viewpoint overlooking the harbour

Stage 2: Porthleven to Rinsey Head From the cliff-top, continue east along the coastal path Keep the sea on your right as you walk along the cliffs Pass Porthleven Head with excellent views back to the harbour Follow the well-marked path through coastal grassland Watch for seabirds including razorbills and guillemots The path descends slightly then climbs again Arrive at Rinsey Head with panoramic ocean views

Stage 3: Rinsey Head to Praa Sands Continue along the coastal path heading east The cliffs become more dramatic with stunning rock formations Follow the path as it descends towards Praa Sands You'll see the golden beach below you Continue down the sandy path towards the beach Arrive at Praa Sands beach - excellent spot for a swim or lunch break

Return Journey: Praa Sands to Porthleven From Praa Sands beach, climb back up the coastal path Retrace your steps back past Rinsey Head Continue west along the cliffs back towards Porthleven Pass through the coastal grassland Descend back to the harbour area Return to the car park

fields.title: Bedruthan Steps to Watergate Bay Coastal Adventure
fields.description:
Experience one of Cornwall's most iconic coastal landscapes on this dramatic clifftop walk. Bedruthan Steps is famous for its towering sea stacks - massive rock formations that rise 60 metres from the beach like giant stepping stones. This spectacular route combines rugged coastal scenery, hidden coves, and panoramic Atlantic views. The walk takes you past the National Trust-owned Bedruthan Steps, along dramatic cliffs with breathtaking geology, and down to the expansive Watergate Bay with its golden sands and excellent surf conditions. Perfect for photographers, nature lovers, and adventure seekers.

Walking Directions:

Stage 1: Bedruthan Steps Car Park to The Stepping Stones Viewpoint Start at Bedruthan Steps National Trust car park Take the main coastal path heading north Follow the well-marked path along the clifftop Keep the sea on your right throughout Pass the information board about the rock formations Arrive at the main Bedruthan Steps viewpoint Stop to admire the massive sea stacks rising from the beach below The rocks are said to be stepping stones used by a giant in Cornish legend.

Stage 2: Bedruthan Steps to Porth Joke Cove Continue north along the coastal path from the viewpoint The path winds through coastal grassland with wildflowers Follow the blue and white coastal path waymarkers Pass several smaller rock formations and natural arches The cliffs gradually become steeper and more dramatic Descend slightly as you approach Porth Joke Cove You'll see the secluded cove nestled below the cliffs This is an excellent spot for a rest and photos.

Stage 3: Porth Joke to Watergate Bay From Porth Joke, continue north along the cliff-top path The landscape becomes more rugged with dramatic rockfaces Follow the path as it winds inland slightly through grassland Watch for gorse bushes and coastal flowers (especially in spring) The path curves back towards the sea Descend gradually towards Watergate Bay You'll see the wide sandy beach stretching ahead Continue down the sandy path to reach Watergate Beach Arrive at the expansive Watergate Bay with excellent facilities.

Stage 4: Watergate Bay Exploration Walk along Watergate Beach - one of Cornwall's best beaches Explore the sandy cove and rock pools Visit the beach cafe and facilities if needed This is an ideal lunch spot with great views.

Return Journey: Watergate Bay to Bedruthan Steps From Watergate Beach, retrace your steps back up the coastal path Climb back up towards the cliff-top Continue south past Porth Joke Cove Follow the path back along the dramatic cliffs Pass the Bedruthan Steps viewpoint again Continue south to return to the car park.

fields.title: Tintagel Castle to Boscastle Coastal Trail
fields.description:
An epic coastal walk combining dramatic clifftop scenery with charming fishing villages. Start at the legendary Tintagel Castle ruins and follow the South West Coast Path northward, passing Glebe Cliff and Willapark before descending into the picturesque harbor village of Boscastle. The route features stunning views of the Atlantic, rugged granite cliffs, and interesting rock formations. The return journey offers opportunities to explore both villages properly. This is a moderate to challenging walk with some steep descents and ascents, particularly around Boscastle.


Directions:

Start at Tintagel Castle Car Park – Park here and pay the fee. Head towards the castle entrance.

Walk to Tintagel Castle entrance – Follow signs to the castle ruins. There's a steep descent of steps down to the headland.

Explore castle ruins – Walk around the castle headland. Enjoy views of the Atlantic.

Exit castle and turn north – Head back up and follow signs for the South West Coast Path heading towards Boscastle.

Walk along Glebe Cliff  – Continue on the coastal path with dramatic cliff views on your right. The path is well-marked with acorn symbols.

Pass Willapark – Continue following the coast path, heading downhill at times.

Descend into Boscastle Harbour  – The path descends steeply into the village. Follow signs for the High Street.

Explore Boscastle village – Visit the harbor, grab lunch or a drink at a local pub, explore the shops and galleries.

Return journey – Retrace your steps back to Tintagel Castle the same way, taking the same steep climbs and descents.

fields.title: Porthtowan to Ralph's Cupboard Loop
fields.description:
A spectacular circular coastal walk combining golden sandy beaches with dramatic clifftop views. Starting from Porthtowan Beach, follow the South West Coast Path eastward past Chapel Porth and Trevaunance Cove, enjoying stunning Atlantic vistas and mining heritage sites. The route passes through coastal farmland and quiet country lanes, with opportunities to visit traditional fishing coves. Return via inland paths through moorland and pastoral scenery, offering contrast to the dramatic coastline. Well-marked throughout with moderate terrain and several small hills. Perfect for photographers and nature lovers seeking an authentic Cornish coastal experience.


Walking Steps:

  1. Start at Porthtowan Beach Car Park – Park and head to the beach.
  2. Walk along Porthtowan Beach – Head east along the sand towards the cliffs (~0.5 km).
  3. Climb to coastal path – Follow the South West Coast Path heading northeast.
  4. Pass Chapel Porth (~2.5 km) – Enjoy clifftop views and visit the old mining engine house.
  5. Continue to Trevaunance Cove (~4 km) – Another historic mining cove with excellent views.
  6. Reach Ralph's Cupboard (~5.5 km) – A natural rock formation and scenic viewpoint.
  7. Turn inland – Leave the coast path and head south through farmland on country lanes.
  8. Walk through moorland (~7 km) – Peaceful inland section with open views.
  9. Return via quiet lanes (~9 km) – Follow farm tracks and quiet roads back towards Porthtowan.
  10. Return to car park (~10.8 km) – Arrive back at Porthtowan Beach.

fields.title: Perranporth to Watergate Bay Epic Coastal Trek
fields.description:
Description: An epic full-day coastal odyssey following the South West Coast Path from the golden sands of Perranporth to the surf destination of Watergate Bay. This challenging trek combines dramatic granite cliffs, hidden coves, windswept headlands, and charming beach villages. The route passes through diverse landscapes including Perranporth Beach, St Agnes Head (with its distinctive red and white striped lighthouse), Trevaunance Cove, Chapel Porth, Wheal Coates, and finishes at the expansive Watergate Bay. Expect constant elevation changes, exposed coastal sections, and stunning Atlantic views. Several facilities available for refreshments in villages along the route. A true test of stamina with rewarding scenery throughout. Best tackled in good weather and early starts advised.

Walking Steps:

  1. Start at Perranporth Beach Car Park (50.3317° N, 5.1083° W) – Arrive early, as this is a full day walk.

  2. Cross Perranporth Beach – Walk across the wide sandy beach heading north (~0.5 km).

  3. Climb to coastal path – Join the South West Coast Path heading northeast along cliffs.

  4. Pass Droskyn Point (~2 km) – Dramatic headland with views back towards Perranporth.

  5. Reach Ligger Point (~3.5 km) – Continue with clifftop walking, stunning Atlantic views.

  6. Arrive at St Agnes Head (5 km) – Iconic red and white striped lighthouse. This is a major landmark. Rest here (15-20 min).

  7. Descend to Trevaunance Cove (~6.5 km) – Beach and village with cafes and shops. Good opportunity for lunch break.

  8. Climb out of cove – Steep ascent back to clifftop level (~7.5 km).

  9. Walk to Chapel Porth (~8.5 km) – Historic mining cove, old engine house visible. Another chance to rest.

  10. Continue along cliffs – Pass Wheal Coates mining site (~10 km).

  11. Walk through Mawgan Porth headland section (~12-13 km) – Exposed, windswept section with excellent views.

  12. Descend to Mawgan Porth Beach (~13.5 km) – Small village with facilities if needed.

  13. Ascend cliffs again – Continue northeast on coastal path (~14 km).

  14. Pass Watergate Bay headland (~17 km) – Cross high cliffs overlooking the bay.

  15. Descend steeply into Watergate Bay (~20 km) – Long descent to the beach level.

  16. Walk along Watergate Bay Beach – Finish at the beach or car park area (~22.5 km).


    Tips:

    • Start by 8:00 AM latest
    • Bring plenty of water and energy snacks
    • Wear waterproof jacket (coastal weather changes quickly)
    • Sturdy hiking boots essential for rocky sections
    • Apply sunscreen – cliffs offer no shade
    • Download offline maps (no mobile signal in places)
    • Consider arranging transport back from Watergate Bay to Perranporth
    • Several villages en-route offer food/drink stops

    This is a serious undertaking – only suitable for experienced hikers in good fitness!

fields.title: Bodmin Moor Circular Loop
fields.description:
Description: A spectacular inland moorland walk exploring the rugged beauty of Bodmin Moor, Cornwall's largest area of open moorland. This circular route climbs to Rough Tor, the second highest peak on the moor with ancient cairns and panoramic views, then continues to Brown Willy, Cornwall's highest point. Begin from the peaceful village of Bolventor, ascending through heather moorland peppered with prehistoric stone circles, settlement ruins, and Bronze Age burial cairns. The landscape shifts between open moorland, rocky outcrops, and sheltered valleys. Excellent wildlife spotting opportunities including Dartford warblers and adders. On clear days, views extend to Bodmin town, Lisllevegh, and towards Exmoor. A challenging but rewarding inland adventure showcasing geological heritage and wild Cornish countryside.

Walking Steps:

  1. Start at Bolventor village car park (50.5667° N, 4.7167° W) – Small moorland village. Head towards the moor.

  2. Follow moorland track northward – Leave village and head onto open moorland (~0.5 km).

  3. Ascend towards Rough Tor – Steadily climb the moorland slope with heather and grass (~2 km).

  4. Reach Rough Tor summit (3 km) – Ancient cairns visible. Panoramic views of surrounding moor. Rest here (15 min).

  5. Descend towards Showery Tor – Head southwest across open moorland (~4.5 km).

  6. Pass prehistoric stone circles – Walk past ancient Bronze Age remains and settlement ruins (~5.5 km).

  7. Climb towards Brown Willy – Ascend to Cornwall's highest peak at 420m (~7 km).

  8. Reach Brown Willy summit (7.5 km) – Stone cairn at top. Rest and enjoy 360° views (15 min).

  9. Descend southwestward – Head down towards De Lank River valley (~8.5 km).

  10. Walk through sheltered valley – Follow small stream through moorland vegetation (~9.5 km).

  11. Return to moorland track – Head back towards Bolventor following marked paths (~10.5 km).

  12. Return to village car park (~11.2 km).

fields.title: Goss Moor Nature Reserve Gentle Loop
fields.description:
Description: A peaceful and accessible walk through Goss Moor Nature Reserve, perfect for families, beginners, and those seeking a leisurely stroll. This gentle circular route follows well-maintained paths through heathland and wetland habitats, with excellent opportunities for birdwatching and wildflower spotting. The terrain is mostly flat with minimal elevation gain, and multiple benches are scattered throughout for resting and enjoying the natural surroundings. The reserve is home to numerous species including stonechats, linnets, and rare dragonflies. Ideal for a relaxing afternoon, early morning walk, or quality time with family. Excellent interpretation boards explain the local ecology and conservation efforts. Suitable for all ages and fitness levels.

Walking Steps:

  1. Start at Goss Moor car park (50.4517° N, 4.8483° W) – Free parking available. Pick up a reserve guide if available.

  2. Enter reserve via main gate – Follow the well-marked main path heading into the reserve (~0.3 km).

  3. Walk through heathland section – Flat path with heather on both sides. Early morning is best for birdwatching (~1 km).

  4. Reach first viewing platform (~1.5 km) – Rest here and look for birds and dragonflies in the wetland below.

  5. Continue on loop path – Gentle walking through mixed habitat (~2.5 km).

  6. Pass through woodland section – Shaded flat path through trees (~3.2 km).

  7. Reach second rest bench (~3.5 km) – Peaceful spot to sit and enjoy nature.

  8. Return towards car park – Follow signs back on easy flat paths (~4.2 km).

  9. Arrive back at car park (~4.5 km).

fields.title: Polurrian Cove Clifftop Stroll
fields.description:
Description: A delightful short coastal walk perfect for a quick escape or sunset visit. This easy clifftop route explores the picturesque Polurrian Cove with its dramatic granite rocks and turquoise waters. The walk features stunning Atlantic views, interesting rock formations, and abundant seabirds. The path is well-maintained and safe for families. Start from the small car park overlooking the cove and follow the clifftop path with interpretive boards explaining the local geology. The cove is popular with swimmers and rock poolers in summer. An ideal quick walk for those with limited time who still want to enjoy authentic Cornish coastal beauty.


Walking Steps:

  1. Start at Polurrian Cove car park (50.0517° N, 5.2583° W) – Small parking area overlooks the cove.

  2. Exit car park towards clifftop – Short path leads to viewing areas (~0.1 km).

  3. Walk along clifftop path eastward – Flat, well-maintained path with safety railings. Views of rocky cove below (~0.5 km).

  4. Reach eastern clifftop viewpoint (~0.7 km) – Best vantage point for photos. Rest here and enjoy the view.

  5. Return back along same path – Retrace your steps (~1.4 km).

fields.title: St Mary’s Coastal Circuit
fields.description:
Description: A beautiful island coastal loop around St Mary’s, the largest of the Isles of Scilly. This relaxed circuit passes sandy coves, turquoise shallows, and granite headlands with constant sea views. Highlights include Porthcressa Beach, the Garrison walls and viewpoints, Peninnis Head, Old Town Bay, and the peaceful dunes at Porth Hellick. The route is mostly easy with a few gentle climbs around the headlands, and the paths are well-marked. Ideal for a full day of slow-paced exploration, swimming, and photo stops. Spectacular on clear days with views across the archipelago.

Walking Steps:

  1. Start at Hugh Town – Begin near the harbour and follow the coastal path east past Porthcressa Beach.
  2. Climb to the Garrison – Walk the historic Garrison walls for panoramic views over the harbour and islands.
  3. Head south to Peninnis Head – Follow the path along dramatic cliffs with open Atlantic views.
  4. Continue to Old Town Bay – Descend to the sandy bay and stroll through Old Town.
  5. Walk to Porth Hellick – Follow quiet lanes and coastal paths to the sheltered bay and dunes.
  6. Turn north along Bar Point – Follow the shoreline with views to Tresco and Bryher.
  7. Return to Hugh Town – Complete the loop along the north shore back to the harbour.

fields.title: Swanpool Beach to Maenporth Coastal Walk
fields.description:
Description: A picturesque coastal walk starting from the sheltered Swanpool Beach, one of South Cornwall's most beautiful sandy coves. The route follows the South West Coast Path eastward through woodland and along dramatic clifftops, passing Maenporth Beach and exploring hidden coves. The walk offers stunning views across Falmouth Bay with opportunities to spot seabirds and marine wildlife. Swanpool is a thriving ecosystem with a freshwater lagoon separated from the sea by a sandy bar. The return journey retraces the coast path through peaceful woodland with shade and shelter. Perfect for a leisurely half-day outing combining beach, cliff, and woodland scenery.

Walking Steps:

  1. Start at Swanpool Beach car park – Park at the main car park and head to the beach.

  2. Walk along Swanpool Beach – Explore the sandy cove and freshwater lagoon area (~0.5 km).

  3. Climb to coastal path – Follow the South West Coast Path heading east with clifftop views.

  4. Pass through woodland – Shaded path through trees with occasional cliff views (~2 km).

  5. Reach Maenporth Beach – Descend to the sandy beach with dramatic orange cliffs behind (~3.5 km).

  6. Explore Maenporth – Rest and enjoy the beach (~15 min).

  7. Return along same route – Retrace your steps back to Swanpool through the woodlands and coastal path (~7.8 km).

fields.title: Land's End to Sennen Cove Clifftop
fields.description:
Description: An exhilarating expert-level coastal walk tackling the dramatic and exposed cliffs at England's most famous headland. This challenging route combines steep terrain, exposed clifftop paths, and Atlantic exposure with stunning scenery across the Longships Lighthouse and the Celtic Sea. Starting from iconic Land's End, the walk heads north along the South West Coast Path through some of the Southwest's most rugged and windswept landscape. The route features numerous elevation changes, narrow cliff-edge sections, scrambling opportunities, and sections where you'll feel the full force of Atlantic weather. Sennen Cove's golden beach offers a rewarding respite before the challenging return journey. Only suitable for experienced walkers with excellent fitness and head for heights. Avoid in poor weather or high winds.


Walking Steps:

  1. Start at Land's End car park – Begin at the iconic signpost and head north on the coast path.

  2. Climb Greeb Cliffs – Steep initial ascent with exposure. Strong winds common in this section (~1 km).

  3. Traverse exposed clifftop – Narrow path with sheer drops on the right. Concentration essential (~2 km).

  4. Pass Longships Lighthouse viewpoint – Dramatic views. The lighthouse sits on rocks offshore (~3 km).

  5. Navigate Porthcurnick section – Scrambling over rocks and exposed ledges. Requires sure-footedness (~4 km).

  6. Cross Priest's Cove – Narrow descents and ascents through dramatic rock formations (~5 km).

  7. Reach Chapel Carn Brea – Ancient stone cairn with panoramic views across the coast (~6 km).

  8. Drop to Sennen Cove – Long descent to the beautiful sandy beach. Rest break (~7 km).

  9. Return via same route – Challenging return with significant elevation, especially the final climbs back to Land's End (~13.4 km).

Safety warnings:

  • Expose clifftop sections – stay back from edges
  • Weather-dependent – strong winds frequent
  • No shade or shelter on exposed sections
  • Mobile signal unreliable
  • Loose rocks and scree common
  • Tides affect beach access at Sennen

fields.title: Padstow Estuary Loop via Rock
fields.description:
Description: A scenic coastal walk combining river estuary views with sandy beaches and charming harbour villages. Starting from picturesque Padstow, famous for its fishing industry and seafood restaurants, the route crosses the Camel Estuary via stepping stones or ferry to reach the quieter village of Rock. The return journey follows woodland paths and quiet lanes through the North Cornwall countryside, offering contrast to the bustling waterfront. Excellent wildlife spotting—egrets, herons, and oystercatchers frequent the estuary. The route passes through St Enodoc Church's hidden valley and offers views across Padstow Bay. Perfect for a leisurely full-day walk combining estuary, village, and countryside scenery. Good cafés and pubs available in both Padstow and Rock.

Walking Steps:

  1. Start at Padstow Harbour Car Park – Explore the working fishing harbour and waterfront.

  2. Walk along North Quay – Follow the estuary path with views upstream (~0.5 km).

  3. Cross Camel Estuary – Use stepping stones or take the passenger ferry to Rock (~1 km).

  4. Explore Rock village – Small coastal settlement with beach and cafés (~1.5 km).

  5. Head inland – Leave the waterfront and climb into woodland paths.

  6. Visit St Enodoc Church – Hidden tiny church in a valley setting (~4 km).

  7. Follow country lanes – Quiet rural paths through farmland (~6 km).

  8. Return towards Padstow – Cross fields and lanes heading back west (~8 km).

  9. Arrive back at Padstow – Complete the loop at the harbour (~9.4 km).

fields.content: This was such a good walk! Need to set off early though
I look forward to completing this walk.
